clue.text: About to introduce man who's acting head of state

indicators.note: the first piece comes before and so ushers in the next one in the answer

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
a gent is a man, short for gentleman

explanation.surface: A notice about bringing in someone who is standing in as head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to introduce' says RE goes in front of GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules on behalf of a monarch who is a child, absent or unfit, so serves as a stand-in sovereign.

clue.text: Scorn of professional intercepting pass

indicators.note: one piece cuts in on the other, as a defender intercepts a pass

parts.note: to reach something to someone is to pass or hand it
pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: A footballer's disdain for a pro cutting out his pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intercepting' puts PRO inside REACH. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Reproach is disapproval or blame, close in sense to contempt.

clue.text: Sliding scale, perhaps

parts.note: not a pay system but a musical run where a player slides rapidly up or down the notes

explanation.walkthrough: A 'sliding scale' is usually a variable rate of charges; here it is a run of notes played in a slide.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a glissando is a rapid slide through successive notes, as on a harp or piano.

clue.text: Carol's boyfriend?

parts.note: a carol is a Christmas song, and a man's name for its partner would be the French word for Christmas, also a boy's name

explanation.walkthrough: Carol reads as a girl's name; the answer is both a Christmas carol and a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A noel is a Christmas carol, and Noel is a man's name, so it could be the boyfriend of a Carol.

clue.text: Revolutionary financial instrument may be seen as a sting

indicators.note: the letters of the following words may be seen in another arrangement, so they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A banking product of the Revolution turns out to be a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be seen' rearranges the eight letters of AS A STING. 'Revolutionary' means of the French Revolution, not radical.
explanation.definitionFit: Assignats were the paper banknotes issued by the French revolutionary government in the 1790s.

clue.text: Fine line used in poster

indicators.note: the line letter is put to use inside the other word

parts.note: a sender is one who posts something

explanation.surface: A thin line printed on a placard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poster' is one who posts, SENDER, not a placard; 'used in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means thin or fine in build.

clue.text: Rising and cursing yen's instability

indicators.note: an unstable arrangement suggests the letters will tumble into a new order

parts.note: the possessive s gives no letter, leaving yen

explanation.surface: Someone swearing at the yen's wobbles as it climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instability' rearranges CURSING YEN. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgency is a rising, an uprising against authority.

clue.text: 3 introduces British patron of prizes

indicators.note: the Christmas word takes the British letter into itself

parts.note: refers to the answer at 3 down, a Christmas carol

explanation.surface: A carol presenting the British benefactor behind famous awards.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' means the answer to 3 down, NOEL; 'introduces' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel founded the Nobel Prizes in his will.

clue.text: Cloth pattern in brown, full of ingenuity

indicators.note: the brown word is filled with the other piece

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
art can mean skill or cunning ingenuity

explanation.surface: A design woven in brown shows great inventiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts ART inside TAN. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is a woven checked pattern associated with Scottish clans.

clue.text: It's easy to find bill in folder

indicators.note: the bill letters are placed inside the folder word

parts.note: a file is a folder for papers
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Locating an invoice in its folder is no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AC inside FILE. 'It's' and 'to find' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile means achieved with little effort, effortless.

clue.text: Two or three, say, consider cheapest charge for loan

parts.note: two and three are both prime numbers, so these are examples of a prime
to rate something is to consider or regard it

explanation.surface: Someone weighing up two or three of the lowest-cost loan offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks two or three as examples of prime numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The prime rate is the lowest interest rate a bank offers its best borrowers.

clue.text: Like a judge, they say, in tailored robes

indicators.note: tailored means cut and fashioned, so the word robes is cut up and remade

explanation.surface: A judge, so people claim, wears specially made robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailored' rearranges ROBES; the definition leans on the saying 'sober as a judge', which 'they say' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock simile 'sober as a judge' makes the adjective the quality proverbially shared with a judge.

clue.text: Dismiss from university in east of Germany

indicators.note: the university letter sits inside the German word

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: Someone being expelled from a university in eastern Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'east of Germany' is the word for east in German, OST, not a region; 'in' places U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss someone from a post is to remove or expel them.

clue.text: In fairytale, she was a slippery customer

definitions.text: In fairytale, she was a slippery customer

parts.words: In fairytale, she was a slippery customer
parts.note: a slippery customer is normally a crook, but here it is a heroine identified by the glass slipper she leaves behind

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale woman who was a shifty character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippery' means associated with a slipper, not untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of the pantomime story is found by the prince through the glass slipper she lost at the ball.

clue.text: Secret trust

definitions.meaning: something told privately, in the sense of a thing said in strict privacy
firm belief or faith in someone

explanation.definitionFit: A confidence is a private disclosure, and confidence is also faith or reliance placed in someone.

clue.text: Sympathise with prisoner receiving benefit

indicators.note: the prisoner piece takes the benefit piece after it in the answer

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Feeling sorry for an inmate who is getting state handouts.
explanation.walkthrough: THE DOLE is everyday British for state unemployment benefit; 'receiving' sets DOLE after CON. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To condole is to express sympathy with someone in grief.

clue.text: Bubbly city where there's lots written, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word for lots written is spoken, matching the city's sound

parts.note: reams are large quantities of written material

explanation.surface: A champagne town where writers have produced a vast amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' matches REAMS with RHEIMS, the English spelling of Reims. 'Bubbly' means champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Reims is a capital of the Champagne region, home to great champagne houses.

clue.text: Quarter in which one's uncomfortably near foreign legionnaire, say

indicators.note: the quarter word holds the scrambled piece within it

parts.note: to give quarter is to show mercy to a defeated enemy

indicators.note: near arranged in an uncomfortable, awkward way is to be reordered

explanation.surface: A foreign legionnaire finds himself in a district too close for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter' is mercy shown to a beaten foe, not a district; 'uncomfortably' rearranges NEAR into ENAR, which goes 'in' MERCY. 'one's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercenary is a soldier hired by a foreign power, as members of the French Foreign Legion are an example.

clue.text: One minute with stout businessman

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
porter is a dark beer like stout

explanation.surface: A short time spent with a heavily built trader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' is the dark beer, not fat. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An importer is a trader who brings goods in from abroad.

clue.text: Covered up little bounder being given a meal

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, an animal that bounds; the shortening gives 'little'
fed means having been given food

explanation.surface: A small rascal is hidden after being given dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounder' is a cad in the surface but a leaping animal in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed building has a covering over the top.

clue.text: Ladies accept silver as compensation

indicators.note: the ladies take in the silver, holding it inside

parts.note: dames are ladies
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Women taking silver as settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accept' puts AG inside DAMES. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Damages are money awarded by a court as compensation for loss or injury.

clue.text: Polite behaviour in Christmas month — no alcohol

parts.note: Dec is the short form of December, the month of Christmas
O, the figure nought, stands for none or no
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: Good manners in December mean staying off the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no alcohol' looks like abstinence but gives O plus RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is propriety and good taste in conduct.

clue.text: As bait, offer head of dragonfly to fish

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod and line

explanation.surface: An angler offers a dragonfly as bait on the hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' takes D from 'dragonfly'. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle something is to hold it out as a temptation, as a lure.

clue.text: Scales only part of this zodiac sign?

definitions.text: Scales only part of this zodiac sign?

parts.words: Scales only part of this zodiac sign?
parts.note: Scales suggests Libra, but here the scales belong to a fish, so they are only part of the creature this sign shows

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scales' points to the sign Libra; it is the scales on fish, which are part of the sign of the Fishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisces, the Fishes, is the twelfth sign of the zodiac, and fish have scales.

clue.text: Part of Greek temple based on one-metre block

indicators.note: the temple part sits on top of the other pieces, which in an across answer means it comes after them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the pediment is the triangular gable above the columns of a classical temple

explanation.surface: Part of an ancient Greek temple rests on a block a metre across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'based on' puts PEDIMENT after I and M; 'block' is the definition, an obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An impediment is an obstruction or hindrance, something that blocks progress.

clue.text: Diarist looks sound

indicators.note: sound here means sounds like, so the spoken word for looks matches the diarist's name

parts.note: peeps are quick looks

explanation.surface: A diary writer's appearance is healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy but means 'sounds like'. Samuel Pepys, whose name is said PEEPS, kept a famous 17th-century London diary.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys wrote the best-known English diary, covering the 1660s.

clue.text: March sees half the characters in Greenwich attraction changing places

indicators.note: two of the word's four letters are the ones involved in the swap
the two chosen letters swap positions with each other

parts.note: the Millennium Dome at Greenwich in London, now the O2 arena

explanation.surface: A procession sees some of the staff at a Greenwich venue swapping jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: The O and the E of DOME, half its letters, swap places to give DEMO. The Dome is the large tent-like arena at Greenwich in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo, short for demonstration, is a protest march.

clue.text: This first for patient that's out of sorts?

definitions.text: This first for patient that's out of sorts?

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word patient is used

parts.note: unwell or ill

explanation.surface: A tablet is the first thing given to a patient who is under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes P from 'patient', and ILL follows; the whole clue describes a remedy for a sick patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is a tablet of medicine given to someone unwell.

clue.text: Chicken — evidence it's not headless?

definitions.meaning: a castrated cockerel fattened for the table
having a ... shows there is a head to wear it

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as CAP ON: a cap is worn on a head, so it proves one is there.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated male fowl, and a cap on suggests a head below it.

clue.text: Impudence — Russian taking time to be flirtatious

parts.note: gall is cheek or impudence
Ivan is a stock Russian man's name

explanation.surface: A cheeky Russian takes his time over flirting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts T into IVAN, at its end. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant once meant to flirt or play the gallant with women, as well as to gad about.

clue.text: Be aware of us quietly hiding in anxious uncertainty

indicators.note: the outer word conceals the other pieces within it

parts.note: to sense something is to be aware of it
taken as written
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Knowing that we are silently concealing something leaves us on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' puts US and P inside SENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the tense state of waiting uncertainly for an outcome.

clue.text: Competitor's pawn was placed in front of queen

indicators.note: the earlier pieces stand ahead of the queen piece in the answer

parts.note: P is the chess notation for pawn
lay is the past tense of lie, to be placed or situated
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the regular abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A chess player's pawn was moved in front of the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture is a decoy: 'pawn' gives P and 'was placed' gives LAY, set 'in front of' ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a participant in a game or contest.
